data.narrative:
The Spaceport Company is a Seed-stage space and aerospace venture that has raised $2M to date. The valuation assessment draws from a sector universe of 5 public comps (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers, including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and ICEYE.

Of three valuation methods examined, only Stage-Progression proved applicable. This method uses the $2M total raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for Seed-to-next-stage progression, yielding an implied valuation of $5M. Peer-Median analysis was not executable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the Space & Aerospace sector—while 14 same-sector peers exist overall, fewer than three fell within narrow stage or valuation tier filters. Public-Comp Anchoring could not be applied because the target company's revenue is not on file, preventing calculation of a price-to-sales multiple despite the sector median of 27.4x across public comps.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $4M to $6M, centered at $5M. This narrow range reflects reliance on a single applicable method and the early-stage, capital-intensive nature of aerospace ventures where revenue and unit economics remain nascent. Key uncertainties include the absence of direct peer multiples and undisclosed customer commitments or technical milestone data that would inform risk-adjusted stage progression.
